title: Spelling
intro: Two rules explain most Dutch spelling changes: open and closed syllables, and f/v and s/z. You need them for plurals, verb forms and adjectives.

topics.title: Long and short vowels
topics.summary: Why it is man → mannen but maan → manen.

body.p: Dutch spelling looks odd at first: why **man → mannen** but **maan → manen**? It all follows from one rule about syllables. Learn it once and you can spell plurals, verb forms and adjectives.
A syllable that ends in a vowel is **open** (ma-, bo-). A syllable that ends in a consonant is **closed** (man, boom).

list: A **long** vowel in a **closed** syllable is written double: **maan**, **boom**, **straat**.
A **long** vowel in an **open** syllable is written single, because it is long already: **ma-nen**, **bo-men**, **stra-ten**.
A **short** vowel needs a closed syllable. So when an ending with a vowel follows, the consonant is doubled: **man → man-nen**, **bus → bus-sen**, **kat → kat-ten**.

body.tip: The rule only works for **a, e, o, u**. Vowel pairs like **oe, ie, eu, ui, ei, ij, ou, au** never change: boek → boeken, deur → deuren.

mistakes.why: kat has a short a, so the t is doubled to keep the syllable closed.
maak is one closed syllable with a long a, so you write aa.

exercises.why: bo-men: the first syllable is open, so one o is already long.
bus has a short u, so the s is doubled: bus-sen.
loop is a closed syllable with a long o, so you write oo.

exercises.en: I live in a white house.
exercises.why: wit has a short i; adding -e needs a double t: wit-te.
stra-ten: open syllable, so a single a.

topics.title: f/v and s/z
topics.summary: A Dutch word never ends in v or z: leven → ik leef, huis → huizen.

body.p: Dutch words never end in **v** or **z**. At the end of a word you write **f** or **s**. When an ending with a vowel follows, the sound often becomes **v** or **z** again.
For verbs the rule never fails: the stem ends in **f** or **s**, never in v or z. **geven → ik geef**, **reizen → ik reis**, **geloven → ik geloof**.

With nouns it usually works after a long vowel (huis → huizen, brief → brieven), but not always: **de kous → de kousen**, **de fotograaf → de fotografen**. After a short vowel there is no change: **de les → de lessen**.

mistakes.why: A word cannot end in v.
Between two vowels the s-sound of huis becomes z.

exercises.why: A verb stem never ends in v: geef.
Between vowels f becomes v: brieven.
A word cannot end in z: reis.
